/bin/bash -lc 'set -euo pipefail
files=(
  MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivRepClassifyZarAffLocal.lean
  MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivRepClassifyZarAffCompat.lean
  MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivRepClassifyZarAff.lean
  MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivRepClassifyZarAffNaturality.lean
)
while true; do
  old=$("$HORIZON_GIT" rev-parse refs/heads/main)
  idx=$(mktemp /tmp/ajcr-param-core-commit.XXXXXX)
  rm -f "$idx"
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree "$old"
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- "${files[@]}"
  actual=$(GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" "$HORIZON_GIT" diff --cached --name-only "$old" | sort)
  expected=$(printf '"'%s\\n' \""'${files[@]}" | sort)
  test "$actual" = "$expected"
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" "$HORIZON_GIT" diff --cached --check "$old"
  tree=$(GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" "$HORIZON_GIT" write-tree)
  new=$(printf '"'%s\\n' 'feat(picard): generalize affine divisor classifier core' | \""'$HORIZON_GIT" commit-tree "$tree" -p "$old")
  if "$HORIZON_GIT" update-ref refs/heads/main "$new" "$old"; then
    printf '"'OLD=%s\\nNEW=%s\\n' \""'$old" "$new"
    GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" "$HORIZON_GIT" diff --cached --name-status "$old"
    GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" "$HORIZON_GIT" diff --cached --stat "$old"
    rm -f "$idx"
    break
  fi
  rm -f "$idx"
done'

104:## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there
105-
106:`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
107-directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
108:that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
109:path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
110-15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:
111-
112-```bash
113:LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
114:while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
115-  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
116-  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
117-  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
118-  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
119-    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
120-    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
121-      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
122-    fi
123:    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
124-    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
125-       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
126-      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
127-    fi
128-  fi
129-  sleep 10
130-done
131-echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
132:# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
133-```
134-
135:### 2a. THE RELEASE IS AS DANGEROUS AS THE REAP — check the pidfile before `rm -rf` (2026-07-28, run 0072)
136-
137-The acquire loop above is careful; the release (`rm -rf "$LOCK"`) is not, and that asymmetry
138:caused a real incident. **A lane removed the lock directory while its pidfile named a LIVE pid
139-belonging to another lane's build**, having printed `ALIVE` for that pid one line earlier.
140-
141-The mechanism is worth stating because nothing in the recipe warns about it. The offending lane
142-had legitimately acquired the lock, and then **its own shell was killed by a harness timeout
143-while it held it**. On the next turn it reasoned "the lock is mine and my holder is dead, so
144-release it" — but in the interval a *different* lane had acquired the lock, so the pid in the
145-file had never been its own. The lane was running the release branch on a belief about history
146-rather than on a reading of the file.
147-
148:> **Before `rm -rf "$LOCK"`, verify the pidfile still names YOUR pid.**
149-> `[ "$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)" = "$$" ] && rm -rf "$LOCK"`
150-> If it names anything else, the lock is not yours to release: say so and leave it alone.
151-
152-Two corollaries:
153-
154-* **"It was mine a minute ago" is not evidence**, especially when a harness can kill the shell
155-  between acquire and release. Every turn boundary is a window for another lane to take the lock.
156-* **Do not "repair" the mistake by re-creating the directory with the other lane's pid.**
157:  Fabricating a pidfile for a build you do not own makes the lock unreapable by its real owner
158-  and hides the incident. Report it on the thread and let the owner re-take it.
159-
160-For long builds, prefer a form that cannot outlive its own hold: run the build detached with a
161-release trailing it in the *same* script, so the release is not a separate turn.
162-
163-Two stale shapes, both now handled above (do NOT just `sleep` forever on either):
164:- A plain FILE at the lock path is by definition stale (mkdir makes directories) — reap immediately.
165-- An orphaned DIRECTORY from a build that crashed before `rm -rf` (the 2026-07-19 C4 incident,
166-  I-0257): the OLD acquire loop only checked for a file, so it spun forever on this. Writing
167-  `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` on acquire lets the next lane prove the holder is dead (`kill -0`) and reap
168:  safely; the no-pidfile branch (a holder from before this fix) falls back to "no live build + >15min".
169:  Never reap a directory whose pidfile names a LIVE pid — that is a real build in progress.
170-
171-## 3. /tmp quota with >3 lanes
172-
173-uid-1001 tmpfs quota exhaustion (EDQUOT) bricked every Bash call machine-wide
174-(~19:00–19:20). With more than ~3 concurrent lanes, keep scratch artifacts small, clean up
175-build temp dirs, and if Bash starts failing with quota errors, stop and report rather than
176-retry-looping.
177-
178-## 4. The root import file: commit only your own lines (I-0153)
179-
180-`AlgebraicJacobian.lean` is edited by every lane. Committing the WHOLE file via any recipe
181-sweeps siblings' uncommitted import lines into HEAD — the root then references files not yet
182-in HEAD (red for fresh checkouts), and a later sibling's whole-file commit can sweep or drop
183-YOUR line the same way. Before committing the root file: run
184-`git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD -- <project>/AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — if lines
185-other than yours differ, either (a) verify every swept import's file is already committed in
186-HEAD and say so in the commit message, or (b) construct the commit from HEAD's version plus
187-only your lines (apply a minimal patch to a temp checkout of the HEAD blob). Never commit a
188-root file that references uncommitted files without naming that in the message.
189-
190-### 4a. A MINUS line in that diff is never yours (2026-07-28, run 0072)
191-
192-The check above works. The failure mode is **misreading** it, and it happened again on
193-2026-07-28: the diff printed a `-import`/`+import` pair from a sibling lane's *uncommitted*
194-worktree edit, the committing lane read it as background noise, and the commit published the
195-sibling's replacement — dropping `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` from the import closure.
196-The file stayed in HEAD and still compiled, but was reachable from nothing: **un-rooted**,
197-i.e. I-0153 again, from a lane that had run the I-0153 check.
198-
199-So state the rule in a form that needs no judgement:
200-
201-> **A `-import` line in that diff is never yours.** The only clean result is `+import <your
202-> file>` and nothing else. Any minus line means you are about to delete another lane's root
203-> entry — stop and explain it before committing. An unexplained `+import` you did not write
204-> is the same signal: a sibling's uncommitted edit is in your worktree copy, and a minus line
--
206-
207-This is strictly stronger than "commit only your own lines", because you can intend that and
208-still sweep — staging the whole file is what publishes their edit, and the diff is your only
209-warning.
210-
211-**Repair additively, never by reverting.** Restore the dropped import while **keeping** the
212-other lane's new one, then verify with a full root build (the 2026-07-28 repair: 9139 jobs,
213-exit 0, with the un-rooted file rebuilt). Reverting to your own earlier root blob discards
214-their work and turns one incident into two.
215-
216:## 5. The AJCR mutex is for AJCR lake invocations only
217-
218-No cross-workspace use (an OpenGA-Horizon agent squatted it ~25 min for its own
219-`lake cache get`, silently serializing AJCR lanes against unrelated work). Other
220-workspaces must use their own lock paths.
221-
222-### 5a. Read it as per-PROJECT, not per-workspace (2026-07-28, run 0072)
223-
224-The rule above says "cross-workspace", and that wording has a hole: **AJC and AJCR are two
225:projects in the SAME workspace.** Observed live on 2026-07-28 — the AJCR mutex was held for
226-over ten minutes while the only live `lake build` belonged to an `ajc-*` lane building
227-`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, the sibling project. Same failure as the
228-OpenGA incident, not covered by the rule as written.
229-
230-The lock path is `ajcr-locks`, so read the rule as: **only lanes building
231-`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` may take it.** AJC lanes need their own path
232:(`/tmp/claude-1001/ajc-locks/lake.lock`). Note the AJC task prompts do not mention a mutex
233-at all, which is very likely why an AJC lane reached for this one.
234-
235:### 5b. Write the pidfile — the no-pidfile fallback cannot distinguish squatter from orphan
236-
237-§2's acquire recipe writes `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` so a later lane can prove death via
238:`kill -0`. In the incident above the lock directory had **no pidfile**, so that branch could
239-not fire and the fallback ("no live `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` **and** dir >15 min old")
240-also could not fire — there *was* a live build, just not an AJCR one. Net effect: a
241-provably-non-AJCR holder is unreapable for 15 minutes.
242-
243-Two consequences for a blocked lane, both applied in that incident:
244-
245-* **Do not reap a directory whose holder you cannot prove dead**, even when you suspect a
246-  squatter. Reaping mid-build is worse than waiting.
247-* **Fall back to the narrowest check instead of blocking.** `lake env lean <file>` on the
248-  single changed file writes no shared build state and needs no lock; it is a faithful
249:  kernel check for that file. Record in the report that the mutex was unavailable and which
250-  check you substituted.

ROOT=/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon

IDX=$(mktemp /tmp/ajcr-param-index.XXXXXX)
trap '"'rm -f \""'$IDX"'"' EXIT
attempt=1
while [ \""'$attempt" -le 8 ]; do
  OLD=$("$HORIZON_GIT" rev-parse HEAD)
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$IDX" "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree "$OLD"
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$IDX" "$HORIZON_GIT" add --     "$PROJECT/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivRepClassifyZarAffSep.lean"     "$PROJECT/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivRepGlobalClassifyAff.lean"     "$PROJECT/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivRepChartRangeAff.lean"     "$PROJECT/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivRepClassifyZarAffSurj.lean"
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$IDX" "$HORIZON_GIT" diff --cached --check
  TREE=$(GIT_INDEX_FILE="$IDX" "$HORIZON_GIT" write-tree)
  NEW=$(printf '"'%s\\n' 'feat(picard): generalize affine representability descent' | \""'$HORIZON_GIT" commit-tree "$TREE" -p "$OLD")
  if "$HORIZON_GIT" update-ref refs/heads/main "$NEW" "$OLD"; then
    echo "commit=$NEW parent=$OLD"
    "$HORIZON_GIT" diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-status -r "$NEW"
    "$HORIZON_GIT" diff-tree --no-commit-id --shortstat -r "$NEW"
    exit 0
  fi
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
done
echo "CAS failed after retries" >&2
exit 1'

/bin/bash -lc 'set -euo pipefail
LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null
do
  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]
  then
    echo "STALE plain mutex file; removing" >&2
    rm -f "$LOCK"
    continue
  fi
  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]
  then
    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null
    then
      echo "STALE dead mutex holder $holder; reaping" >&2
      rm -rf "$LOCK"
      continue
    fi
    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f '"'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1
    then
      age="'$(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) ))
      if [ "$age" -gt 900 ]
      then
        echo "STALE old mutex directory; reaping" >&2
        rm -rf "$LOCK"
        continue
      fi
    fi
  fi
  sleep 10
done
echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid"
cleanup() {
  if [ "$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)" = "$$" ]
  then
    rm -rf "$LOCK"
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
set -o pipefail
lake build   AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepChartClassUnivAffWindows   AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepChartClassUnivAffFst   AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepChartClassUnivAffSnd   AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepChartClassUnivAffRange   AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepChartClassUnivAffRepresentable   2>&1 | tee /tmp/ajcr-param-universal-build.out'

    21	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    22	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 8
    23	set_option maxRecDepth 16000
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory Opposite
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	open Grassmannian Scheme
    32	
    33	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    34	  Scheme.functionFieldOverModule
    35	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    36	
    37	section Curve
    38	
    39	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    40	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    41	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    42	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi] [IsDominant pi]
    43	
    44	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftDivRepChartClassUnivAffRepresentable :
    45	    C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
    46	
    47	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsIntegral C.left]
    48	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    49	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    50	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
    51	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
    52	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))
    53	variable (g : Nat)
    54	variable (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    55	  (hchi : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : Int))
    56	
    57	section Based
    58	
    59	variable (r1 r2 : Nat)
    60	variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
    61	  ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
    62	variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
    63	  ↥(divisorSections k
    64	    ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
    65	
    66	local notation "DivOver" =>
    67	  divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    68	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
    69	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)
    70	
    71	include hO hchi in
    72	/-- For nonzero genus, the universal widened chart classes represent the divisor functor by
    73	the existing divisor scheme. -/
    74	noncomputable def divFunctorAff_representableBy_divScheme_of_ne_zero (hg : g ≠ 0) :
    75	    (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy DivOver := by
    76	  let hb := windowBound_pos_of_genus_ne_zero pi hpi g hg hO hchi
    77	  exact divFunctorAff_representableBy_of_chartClause hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
    78	    (fun i j => PointwiseAchiever.divFamZarAffUniv C hpi g r1 r2 b1
    79	      (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j hO hchi hb)
    80	    (fun i j => PointwiseAchiever.isDivRepClassifyAff_divFamZarAffUniv
    81	      C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 hO hchi i j hb)
    82	
    83	include hO in
    84	/-- At independent curve parameter `gamma ≤ g`, the universal widened chart classes
    85	represent the degree-`g` divisor functor by the existing divisor scheme. -/
    86	noncomputable def divFunctorAff_representableBy_divScheme_at
    87	    {gamma : Nat} (hgamma : gamma ≤ g)
    88	    (hchiGamma : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (gamma : Int)) :
    89	    (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy DivOver :=
    90	  divFunctorAff_representableBy_of_chartClause_at
    91	    hpi g hO hgamma hchiGamma r1 r2 b1 b2
    92	    (fun i j => PointwiseAchiever.divFamZarAffUniv_at C hpi g r1 r2 b1
    93	      (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j hgamma hchiGamma)
    94	    (fun i j => PointwiseAchiever.isDivRepClassifyAff_divFamZarAffUniv_at
    95	      C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j hgamma hchiGamma)
    96	
    97	end Based
    98	
    99	include hO hchi in
   100	/-- The widened divisor functor has a representer in every genus.  The finite chart bases are
   101	chosen internally; genus zero is represented by the terminal object. -/
   102	noncomputable def divFunctorAffRepresenter :
   103	    Σ D : Over (Spec (.of k)), (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy D := by
   104	  classical
   105	  by_cases hg : g = 0
   106	  · subst g
   107	    exact ⟨Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
   108	      divFunctorAffZeroRepresentableBy (C := C) (pi := pi)⟩
   109	  · let r1 := Module.finrank k
   110	      ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)
   111	    let r2 := Module.finrank k ↥(divisorSections k
   112	      ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)
   113	    let b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
   114	        ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤) :=
   115	      Module.finBasis k _
   116	    let b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k ↥(divisorSections k
   117	        ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤) :=
   118	      Module.finBasis k _
   119	    exact ⟨divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
   120	        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
   121	        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm),
   122	      divFunctorAff_representableBy_divScheme_of_ne_zero
   123	        C hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 hg⟩
   124	
   125	include hO in
   126	/-- The degree-`g` widened divisor functor has a chosen representer when the curve Euler
   127	parameter is any `gamma ≤ g`. The degree-zero branch remains the terminal object. -/
   128	noncomputable def divFunctorAffRepresenter_at
   129	    {gamma : Nat} (hgamma : gamma ≤ g)
   130	    (hchiGamma : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (gamma : Int)) :
   131	    Σ D : Over (Spec (.of k)), (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy D := by
   132	  classical
   133	  by_cases hg : g = 0
   134	  · subst g
   135	    exact ⟨Over.mk (𝟏 (Spec (.of k))),
   136	      divFunctorAffZeroRepresentableBy (C := C) (pi := pi)⟩
   137	  · let r1 := Module.finrank k
   138	      ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)
   139	    let r2 := Module.finrank k ↥(divisorSections k
   140	      ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)
   141	    let b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
   142	        ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤) :=
   143	      Module.finBasis k _
   144	    let b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k ↥(divisorSections k
   145	        ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤) :=
   146	      Module.finBasis k _
   147	    exact ⟨divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
   148	        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
   149	        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm),
   150	      divFunctorAff_representableBy_divScheme_at
   151	        C hpi g hO hgamma hchiGamma r1 r2 b1 b2⟩
   152	
   153	/-- A chosen scheme representing the widened divisor functor. -/
   154	noncomputable def divRepAffScheme : Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
   155	  (divFunctorAffRepresenter C hpi g hO hchi).1
   156	
   157	/-- A chosen scheme representing the degree-`g` widened divisor functor at independent
   158	curve parameter `gamma ≤ g`. -/
   159	noncomputable def divRepAffScheme_at {gamma : Nat} (hgamma : gamma ≤ g)
   160	    (hchiGamma : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (gamma : Int)) :
   161	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
   162	  (divFunctorAffRepresenter_at C hpi g hO hgamma hchiGamma).1
   163	
   164	/-- The widened divisor functor is represented by its chosen scheme, with no genus or chart-basis
   165	hypothesis. -/
   166	noncomputable def divFunctorAff_representableBy :
   167	    (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy (divRepAffScheme C hpi g hO hchi) :=
   168	  (divFunctorAffRepresenter C hpi g hO hchi).2
   169	
   170	/-- The degree-`g` widened divisor functor is represented at every independent curve
   171	parameter `gamma ≤ g`. -/
   172	noncomputable def divFunctorAff_representableBy_at
   173	    {gamma : Nat} (hgamma : gamma ≤ g)
   174	    (hchiGamma : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (gamma : Int)) :
   175	    (divFunctorAff C g).RepresentableBy
   176	      (divRepAffScheme_at C hpi g hO hgamma hchiGamma) :=
   177	  (divFunctorAffRepresenter_at C hpi g hO hgamma hchiGamma).2
   178	
   179	end Curve
   180	
   181	end AlgebraicGeometry
